advisory.heading: When you write a sentence
advisory.text: Examine only the rules that you add or change for these cases.
advisory.problem: In /Users/alexk/Projects/agent-context/skills/writing/agent-instructions/references/plain-language-rules.md line 27, "for these cases" can attach to "Examine" or to "add or change", so the reader can read "the rules that you add or change because of these cases".
advisory.correction: "For these cases, examine only the rules that you add or change."

advisory.heading: When you select the text
advisory.text: When the user tells you that an agent did not obey an instruction, make one typical task of the reader test from that problem.
advisory.problem: In skills/writing/agent-instructions/references/plain-language-rules.md line 65, this sentence gives the same instruction as item 1 of "After the self-check: the reader test" in the pointer target review.md line 214 ("If the user told you that an agent did not obey an instruction, make one task from that problem."), and the pointer on line 62 already sends the agent to review.md for the reader test.
advisory.correction: Remove the sentence. Keep "After agents use the file, the edit job examines the text again."

advisory.heading: When you select the text

advisory.heading: When you select the text

advisory.heading: When you select the text
advisory.problem: In skills/writing/agent-instructions/references/plain-language-rules.md line 45, this rule is in the list under "Add one short cause to a rule in each of these cases:" because it changes how an agent usually links files, but no file gives why a sequence of pointers is a problem, for example that an agent can stop before it reads the second pointer target.
